samples.summary: The "Save a copy" recovery action is never exercised — the only test asserts it is NOT called
samples.evidence: `offline-runtime.test.tsx` mocks `recoverOfflineCopy` and the single assertion about it is `expect(recoverOfflineCopy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (line 179, "offers work that could not be saved, without creating anything"). No test ever invokes `toastWarning.mock.calls[0][1].action.onClick`, so the whole hand-back path inside `offerRecoverableWork` is uncovered: the call to `recoverOfflineCopy(store, item, {title, type})`, the three `refused` branches ('empty' / 'unsupported-type' / 'unreadable') that produce the error copy, the incomplete-copy description, the `navigate(getDocumentPath(...))` action, and the `.catch` fallback. `recoverOfflineCopy` itself is tested in `offline-copy-recovery.test.ts`, but nothing proves the runtime ever calls it correctly — and this is the user's only route back to work the SDK could not reconcile, i.e. the whole point of the archive. samples.summary: The Settings offline toggle and its `supportsClientKey()` gate have no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff adds a whole new Settings section: `offlineAvailable = supportsClientKey()` gating the section's existence, plus a `Switch` bound to `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` / `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled`. There is no test file for `app/settings/page.tsx` (glob `packages/frontend/**/settings*` finds no test; grep -i 'settings' over `*.test.*` in packages/frontend returns only unrelated files — workspace-settings, date-format-preference, etc.). The comment in the file states the design rule 'the preference may land early because nothing reads it; the toggle may not' — that rule (hide the switch on a build below `MinClientKeyVersion`) is exactly what is unasserted. The chip's equivalent gate IS tested ('offers nothing on a build that could not honour it'); the Settings one is not. A regression here presents a control promising per-device storage and erasure that the build cannot perform.

samples.summary: `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` wiring into the store is untested, so nothing catches a regression that re-writes documents to the disk the user just cleared
samples.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` builds the store with `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled`, and the comment says it is what stops the still-mounted client putting the open document back on the disk after the toggle is switched off. In `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` `WafflebaseDocStore` is entirely mocked (`captured.push(options)`), and the only option ever read back is `captured[0].onWriteFailure`; nothing asserts `isPersistenceEnabled`. In `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` the store is real and `isOpenElsewhere` IS proven (spy on `session.isOpenInAnyTab`), but `isPersistenceEnabled` is never probed (grep for `isPersistenceEnabled` in `*.test.*` matches only `wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts`, which constructs its own store with its own option). samples.summary: The identity query (`fetchMeOptional`, and the `initialData` seed from the resolved `['me']` cache) is mocked away in every suite, so its two documented hazards are untested
samples.evidence: `collab-document-provider.tsx` documents at length that it must ask with `fetchMeOptional` (because `fetchMe` goes through `fetchWithAuth`, whose 401 arm logs out and hard-redirects every anonymous share-link visitor) and that `initialData: queryClient.getQueryData(['me'])` is what prevents a pending identity causing an attach-then-teardown. Both suites replace the library wholesale: `collab-document-provider.test.tsx` mocks `@tanstack/react-query` with `useQuery: () => ({data: undefined, isPending:false})`, and `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` with `useQuery: () => me`. The `queryFn` therefore never runs and `initialData` is never evaluated, so swapping `fetchMeOptional` back to `fetchMe`, or dropping the seed, fails no test. `shared-document-durability.test.tsx` mocks `CollabDocumentProvider` itself, so it cannot cover this either.
searchedFor: read both collab-document-provider test mocks of @tanstack/react-query

samples.summary: None of the new tooltip copy is asserted — neither the `saved-locally` branch nor the connected/disconnected split of `not-saved`

samples.summary: `isOfflineUser` — the cross-account guard for `removeMember` — has no direct test; it is mocked at its only call site

samples.summary: Two store branches have no test: `dropArchivesWhere`'s `onlyUser` intersection (no caller passes it) and `belongsToAnotherUser`'s orphan-skip
samples.evidence: `dropArchivesWhere(index, range, onlyUser?)` builds a `theirs` key set and filters on it, but both call sites (`dropAllForUser` → `BY_USER`, `collectStale` → `BY_ARCHIVED_AT`) omit the third argument, so the branch is unreachable and untested. samples.summary: 'installs the erase watcher and reads the identity at fire time' asserts only that the first argument is a function

samples.summary: The traversal guard was weakened from 'every request encodes the id' to 'some request does'
samples.evidence: The loop `expect(pathname).toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL))` became `paths.some(...)`, to accommodate `deleteWorkspace`'s new id-less `fetchDocuments` companion call. The `not.toContain('/auth/logout')` check still runs over every URL, so the primary property survives; but a future call that makes two id-carrying requests now passes if only one of them encodes the id. Narrowing to 'at least one path per call carries the encoded id, and no path carries a raw one' is the same accommodation without the loss.

The test that captures the toast options (lines 180-184) destructures only `description` and never reads or invokes `options.action.onClick`. Consequently everything inside the toast action in offline-runtime.tsx:215-255 is unexecuted by any test: the `recoverOfflineCopy(store, item, {title, type})` call, the three `refused` branches ('empty'/'unsupported-type'/'unreadable'), the incomplete-copy description, the `navigate(getDocumentPath(...))` success action, and the `.catch` fallback. verdict.reason: The reviewer's claim holds up under independent search. durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:146 wires `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` into the store, and the comment states this is what stops the still-mounted client re-persisting the open document after the preference is switched off. verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: the provider's identity query (queryFn `fetchMeOptional` and `initialData: () => queryClient.getQueryData(['me'])`, collab-document-provider.tsx:181-188) is never exercised by any test. Both provider suites replace `@tanstack/react-query` entirely (collab-document-provider.test.tsx:32-37 with `useQuery: () => ({data: undefined, isPending:false})` and `getQueryData: () => undefined`; collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:95-98 with `useQuery: () => me` and `getQueryData: () => me.data`), so the queryFn never executes and `initialData` is never evaluated — the durable suite's "waits for the identity" case (line 281) drives `me.isPending` on the mock, which passes with or without the seed. I searched wide for a counterexample: all tests importing CollabDocumentProvider (shared-document-durability.test.tsx:24-31 mocks the component itself; document-detail-lakehouse-tab.test.tsx:39-47 maps both `fetchMe` and `fetchMeOptional` to the same mock so a swap is undetectable; pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx:58-93 uses a real QueryClient but asserts only `initialRoot` with persistence off), every `getQueryData`/`setQueryData` occurrence in test files, every `fetchMe`/`fetchMeOptional` reference in test files, and the absence of any e2e/playwright suite. Nothing fails if `fetchMeOptional` is swapped back to `fetchMe` or the `['me']` seed is dropped. Impact is user-visible (anonymous share-link visitors logged out and redirected to /login; pending identity causing attach-then-teardown that discards the Yorkie change queue), so the gap is major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: The chip's new "turn on offline saving" offer is never clicked by any test
finding.evidence: The diff adds a whole interactive branch: when `offerOffline` is true the chip renders as a `<button onClick={turnOnOfflineSaving}>` (sync-status-chip.tsx:287-303) and the stranded toast gains `action: { label: 'Turn on for later documents', onClick: turnOnOfflineSaving }` (~line 238). `turnOnOfflineSaving` calls `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled(true)` and raises a success toast. The only new test in tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:418-446 reads `warning.mock.calls[0][1].action.label` and asserts wording — it never invokes the handler, never asserts the preference was written, never asserts a success toast, and never asserts the chip becomes a button (or stays a span when the device has already opted in / the build cannot honour it). A broken or unwired handler ships green: the user clicks the design's 'second entry point', nothing is persisted, and they go on believing un-sent work is on disk.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing coverage exists in the same test file. `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:443-465` renders a stranded chip on a capable build, asserts the element is a BUTTON (451), fires a real click (453), and then asserts the preference was actually persisted via the unmocked `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` (456) and that the success toast fired once with honest wording (459-464). Lines 478-493 separately invoke the stranded toast's `action.onClick` and assert the same two effects. The negative branches are covered too: the chip reverts to SPAN once the device has opted in (475) and on a build below the client-key version, where the toast action is asserted `undefined` (495-516). Over-mocking does not apply: only `sonner` and `@yorkie-js/react` are mocked (6-20); the preference module is imported for real (23-26) and is a genuine localStorage-backed store (src/lib/offline-persistence-preference.ts:40-73), so an inert handler or an unrendered button would fail these tests.

finding.summary: Nothing asserts the share route actually wraps itself in NonDurableScope
finding.evidence: `NonDurableScope` is the only thing keeping share-link content off a visitor's disk, and the code says so at length (use-durable-document.ts:44-60, collab-document-provider.tsx docs). The durable suite's case 'never persists anything reached through a share link' (src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx) applies `NonDurableScope` by hand in the test render — it proves the mechanism, not the wiring. A grep for `NonDurableScope` finds it only in use-durable-document.ts, shared-document.tsx, collab-document-provider.tsx and that one test; no test renders `SharedDocumentInner`/the shared route and asserts the scope is present. Delete the wrapper from shared-document.tsx and the whole suite stays green, while a signed-in visitor on somebody's share link gets the durable branch: their own `wb:{userId}:{docKey}` client on their personal Yorkie token, writing shared content to disk past the link's revocation.

verdict.reason: A dedicated route-level test exists: packages/frontend/src/app/shared/__tests__/shared-document-durability.test.tsx renders the real SharedDocumentByToken (shared-document.tsx is not mocked) and, via a CollabDocumentProvider stand-in that calls the real useDurabilityPermitted(), asserts the probe reads 'false' (lines 24-31, 60-81). Since the context default is true (use-durable-document.ts:61,79-81) and only NonDurableScope sets it false (use-durable-document.ts:68-70, applied at shared-document.tsx:1016), deleting the wrapper makes this test fail — precisely the mutation the finding says stays green. A second case (lines 83-90) renders the probe outside the route and asserts 'true', ruling out vacuity. The file is executed: vite.config.ts:452-457 includes src/**/*.test.tsx. The reviewer's grep evidence is inaccurate; this test file also mentions NonDurableScope in its header comment (lines 6, 12).
